masthead.purpose: The nameplate only; uppercase, semi-condensed, with a small raised italic 'The'.

display.purpose: Front-page lead and article titles; condensed, balanced wrap.

title.purpose: Ordinary story headlines in the rail and section stacks.

standfirst.purpose: One-sentence deks under lead, top stories, and article titles.

body-article.purpose: Long-form article paragraphs, 68ch max, display drop cap on the first.

label.purpose: Uppercase Franklin column heads, explainer labels, wire digest head.

meta.purpose: Bylines, read times, ears, utility line, axes, sources; tabular.

figure.purpose: Market values in the markets band; tabular.

motion.name: ease-house
motion.purpose: The single easing for every transition and the edition opening.

motion.name: underline-draw
motion.purpose: Headline underline draws left to right on hover and focus.

motion.name: nav-underline
motion.purpose: Claret 2px nav underline on hover, focus, current page.

motion.name: arrow-nudge
motion.purpose: Continue-reading arrow on hover and focus.

motion.name: wire-underline
motion.purpose: Wire and source link underline darkens from tan to ink.

motion.name: rule-out
motion.purpose: Edition opening: masthead double rule draws from centre.

motion.name: plate
motion.value: clip-path inset(0 0 100% 0) + translateY(.18em) to rest, 760ms ease-house, 240ms + 120ms per line
motion.purpose: Edition opening: lead headline unmasks line by line after the display face loads.

motion.name: settle
motion.value: opacity 0 to 1, 600ms ease-house at 700ms (end dots 300ms ease-out)
motion.purpose: Edition opening: standfirst, wire line, sparkline end dots.

motion.name: plot
motion.value: stroke-dashoffset 1 to 0, 1100ms ease-house, staggered per cell

motion.name: view-transition
motion.value: root out 160ms ease-in; in 300ms ease-house +40ms; named groups 480ms ease-house

motion.name: progress
motion.value: scaleX(var(--p)) updated per animation frame on scroll

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: opening skipped, view transitions off, hover transitions instant

narrative.northStar: The Paper of Record, Played Straight
narrative.overview:
The Daily Spin dresses as a premium financial daily in the Wall Street Journal and Financial Times tradition and never winks. Crisp white newsprint, near-black ink, hairline column rules, a heavy-light double rule under a centred uppercase masthead, and a band of real FRED figures with drawn sparklines give it the gravity of a paper of record; the deadpan satire lives entirely in the words. The craft bar is the real papers themselves, not a generic news portal.

Density is broadsheet density: a three-column front page (briefing, lead, rail), multi-column section grids, a markets table, and a wire digest, all separated by rules rather than whitespace and boxes. Surfaces are flat paper. Hierarchy comes from type weight, width, and rule weight. Article pages narrow to a single 740px reading column with a drop cap, a two-part explainer panel, and, for markets stories, a FRED line chart. Colour is scarce: one claret accent, one oxford blue reserved for data.

Motion is ceremonial and brief: the edition opens once per session (the masthead double rule draws out, the lead headline unmasks line by line, sparklines plot), headlines morph into article titles across page navigations, and hover states draw underlines. All of it yields to `prefers-reduced-motion`.
keyCharacteristics: White paper ground (the owner's choice) with near-black ink.
Three type voices: condensed high-contrast display serif, text serif, Franklin gothic for labels and figures.
Rule weight as hierarchy: 3px ink heads, 1px ink closes, 1px warm-gray hairline separates.
One claret accent; oxford blue only for plotted data; green and red only for change figures.
Flat, square-cornered, shadowless; the only round shapes are data dots.
Tabular lining figures wherever numbers appear.

rules.name: The One Claret Rule
rules.body: Claret is the only accent and marks the paper's own voice: section tags, explainer labels, the number of the day, interaction underlines. It never fills a surface.

rules.name: The Blue Means Data Rule
rules.body: Oxford blue appears only where a real series is plotted. If it is not a FRED line or its end value, it is not blue.

rules.name: The White Ground Rule
rules.body: The page ground is white, the owner's choice after trying the FT-style pink. Never tint it pink, cream or beige; the markets band is the only tinted surface.

rules.name: The Three Voices Rule
rules.body: Display serif for headlines and the nameplate, text serif for anything read as prose, Franklin gothic for anything read as information. A label is never set in serif; a paragraph is never set in gothic.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Every number in Franklin (markets, tables, ears, timestamps, axes) uses tabular numerals so columns of figures align.

rules.name: The Hairline Column Rule
rules.body: Columns are divided by 1px Hairline Tan rules, never by gutters alone or by boxes. When columns stack, the vertical rule becomes a horizontal one.

rules.name: The Rule Weight Rule
rules.body: A 3px Press Ink rule heads a column or section; a 1px Press Ink rule closes a band (nav, markets band, table header, top bar, footer); a 1px Hairline Tan rule separates items within a column. The masthead's 3px-over-1px double rule is the one heavy-light pair.

rules.name: The Flush to the Rule Exception
rules.body: Following newspaper convention, text sits flush against its rules: labels start 8px under the heading rule with no horizontal inset, outer columns carry no outer padding, and ears sit directly between their two ink rules. This is deliberate, not missing padding.

rules.name: The Flat Newsprint Rule
rules.body: Nothing lifts off the page. If an element needs emphasis, give it a heavier rule or a heavier weight, never a shadow.

dos: Do keep the white paper ground on every page; the owner chose it over the FT-style pink.
Do separate columns and items with hairline rules and head them with the 3px ink rule.
Do set every label, figure, byline, and table in Libre Franklin with tabular numerals.
Do run headlines in the condensed display serif with balanced wrapping, and long text in Source Serif 4 capped at 68ch.
Do reserve oxford blue for plotted FRED data and green/red for change figures.
Do keep the original wire headline visible, struck through in claret, and the sources line on every article.
Do gate every animation behind `prefers-reduced-motion` and let the page render in its final state without JavaScript.
donts: Don't add box-shadows, rounded corners, or card backgrounds; the only tinted surface is the markets band and the only circles are data dots.
Don't use claret as a fill or for data, or blue for links.
Don't set labels or section tags above headlines; section tags live in the meta line and byline below.
Don't add photographs, illustrations, or invented logos; there are none to use.
Don't pad text away from its rules to "fix" the flush newspaper setting.
